revised_claims.replaces_allowed_wording: An explicit CM is a dense truth-layout representation over a declared row/column variable split.
revised_claims.allowed_wording: In this repository, an explicit dense CM layout is a dense row-column truth matrix over ordered row variables R and ordered column variables C.
revised_claims.plain_wording: The repository can place every assignment's exact output in a labeled row-column grid.
revised_claims.technical_wording: materialize_cm aligns output axes to the ordered target tuple R+C, broadcasts missing axes, and reshapes the dense Boolean output to (1 << len(R), 1 << len(C)).

sources.locator: materialize_cm target_vars, alignment, broadcast, and final reshape

proposed_claims.allowed_wording: Under the paper's declared X/not-X by Y/not-Y state ordering, each complete two-input Boolean function corresponds to one 2x2 binary operator CM, and Figure 1 enumerates all sixteen.
proposed_claims.plain_wording: Four input cases allow sixteen complete output patterns, so there are sixteen two-input operator matrices.
proposed_claims.technical_wording: A binary function has four ordered input-state pairs and therefore 2^4 possible output patterns; the paper represents each pattern as one complete 2x2 CM.
proposed_claims.scope: originating paper Section 3 and standard Boolean-function counting
proposed_claims.uncertainty: paper-specific state order must remain declared

proposed_claims.allowed_wording: In the originating paper, a logical matrix contains logical expressions and its positive valuation produces the corresponding binary CM.
proposed_claims.plain_wording: An LM holds expressions; positive valuation turns their entries into the bits of a CM.
proposed_claims.technical_wording: Section 4.1 states [Theta] = V_T([M_XThetaY]) and applies V_T entrywise under the LM's declared state ordering.

proposed_claims.allowed_wording: The paper constructs a 4x4 LM for compound four-variable logic through projection, tensor structure, substitution, and modifiers, then obtains a binary 4x4 CM by positive valuation.
proposed_claims.plain_wording: The paper builds the larger logical matrix first and values it into bits afterward.
proposed_claims.technical_wording: Section 5.1's worked expression (W XOR X) implies (not Y AND Z) yields the valued rows 1100, 1110, 0011, 1011 under the paper's declared Y,W by X,Z measurement order.
proposed_claims.uncertainty: ordering and paper notation must remain visible

proposed_claims.allowed_wording: The paper's formal higher-dimensional construction gives a square 2^n by 2^n LM for 2n logical subexpressions and obtains the corresponding CM by valuation.
proposed_claims.plain_wording: The paper's stated general construction grows through square power-of-two matrices.
proposed_claims.technical_wording: Section 5.2 proves the square dimension by induction; the earlier n-factorial/n-by-n introductory wording is not used as the dimensional rule.
proposed_claims.uncertainty: paper contains a separate introductory wording discrepancy

proposed_claims.allowed_wording: A repository matrix coordinate identifies a complete assignment only when R, C, their internal order, the bit-index convention, and relevant fixed-variable context are known.
proposed_claims.plain_wording: A bare row and column number cannot tell you which variables supplied the bits.
proposed_claims.technical_wording: eval_cm_boolean accumulates assignment bits MSB-first in the sequence order supplied by R and C; fixed values participate when an assignment omits a declared variable.
proposed_claims.scope: implemented dense output and lookup contract

proposed_claims.allowed_wording: The repository supports dense layouts of shape 2^|R| by 2^|C|, including rectangular 2x8 and 8x2 layouts; the originating paper does not state this arbitrary rectangular R/C rule as its formal higher-dimensional definition.
proposed_claims.plain_wording: The repository can re-partition one function into rectangles that the paper's general square rule does not define.
proposed_claims.technical_wording: materialize_cm reshapes the aligned target variables to (1 << len(R), 1 << len(C)); Section 5.2 of the paper instead presents a square 2^n by 2^n construction.
proposed_claims.comparator: paper construction versus repository API contract
proposed_claims.uncertainty: repository terminology is a project convention
